AL.name: Alabama
AL.trNote: A trainer has the same access while training; 'trainer' includes a disabled owner training their own animal, someone with 1 year of animal-training experience, or someone credentialed by a service dog school. The animal in training must wear gear (harness, collar, leash, cape or backpack) saying 'service animal in training' that can be read from 20 feet away.
AL.mp: Class C misdemeanor plus 100 hours of community service for a disability organization; a second or later offense is a Class B misdemeanor with a $100 fine
AL.other: Harassing a service animal is a Class C misdemeanor, and injuring or killing one is a Class B or Class A misdemeanor (Ala. Code §§ 13A-11-232 to -234)

AK.name: Alaska
AK.trNote: Only for a trainer employed by, or volunteering with, a school or agency that trains service animals. The animal must wear that school's in-training insignia. This covers only PUBLIC (government-owned) facilities and transit, not private businesses. Blocking a trainer is a violation-level offense (§ 11.76.133).
AK.other: The state access law protects a 'certified service animal' (certified by a training school or facility). Denying access is a Class B misdemeanor (§ 11.76.130(d)).

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.trNote: Any trainer or person with a disability may take an animal being trained as a service animal into a public place for training (§ 11-1024(G)).
AZ.mp: Civil penalty up to $250 per violation
AZ.other: Interfering with, harming or killing a service animal is a crime (A.R.S. § 13-2910)

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.trNote: A dog trainer in the act of training a guide, signal or service dog has the same access, with no extra charge. The statute does not say whether owner-trainers count.
AR.mp: Civil penalty up to $250 per violation (misrepresentation to a public accommodation)
AR.other: Purposely killing or injuring a service animal without just cause is a Class D felony, plus restitution (Ark. Code Ann. § 20-14-304)

CA.name: California
CA.trNote: People with disabilities and licensed or authorized trainers may take dogs they are training as guide, signal or service dogs into public places. The dog must be on a leash and wear an identification tag issued by the county.
CA.mp: Misdemeanor: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both (for knowingly and fraudulently claiming to own or train a guide, signal or service dog)
CA.other: Intentionally injuring or killing a guide, signal or service dog is a misdemeanor (up to $10,000 fine and/or 1 year jail); letting your dog injure one is also penalized (Cal. Penal Code §§ 600.2, 600.5)

CO.name: Colorado
CO.trNote: A trainer, or a person with a disability accompanied by an animal being trained as a service animal, has the same access with no extra charge (§ 24-34-803(2)).
CO.mp: Petty offense: $25 fine for a first offense, $50-$200 for a second, $100-$500 for a third or later. It applies only if the person was warned beforehand and knew the animal was not a service animal.
CO.other: Interfering with, injuring or harming a service animal is unlawful, with criminal penalties and treble civil damages (C.R.S. § 24-34-804). Housing misrepresentation of an assistance animal is covered separately (C.R.S. § 18-13-107.3, civil infraction).

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.trNote: Only for trainers employed by an organization that meets the membership criteria of a professional association of service-animal schools (with photo ID), or volunteers for an organization that trains service animals.
CT.other: Intentionally interfering with a disabled person's use of a service animal is a Class C misdemeanor (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46a-44(d))

DE.name: Delaware
DE.trNote: An individual training a service animal for use by people with disabilities may be accompanied by it in any place of public accommodation. The statute sets no credential requirement.
DE.other: Interfering with a service dog is a Class B misdemeanor, injuring one a Class A misdemeanor, killing one a Class D felony, and stealing one a Class E felony, plus restitution (Del. Code Ann. tit. 16, § 3056F)

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.trNote: A service animal trainer, or the owner of a service animal in training, has the same access. The animal must be at least 6 months old, be undergoing training, be with an experienced trainer or its owner, and wear a harness, backpack or vest marking it as in training (§ 7-1009).
DC.other: Denying or interfering with these access rights is punishable by up to 90 days in jail and/or a $300 fine, or a $250 civil fine (D.C. Code § 7-1007)

FL.name: Florida
FL.trNote: A trainer of a service animal, while engaged in training it, has the same access and liability (§ 413.08(8)). The statute sets no credential requirement.
FL.mp: Second-degree misdemeanor (up to 60 days jail / $500 fine) plus 30 hours of community service for an organization serving people with disabilities
FL.other: Interfering with, injuring or killing a service animal is a crime, up to a third-degree felony for intentional injury or killing, plus restitution (Fla. Stat. § 413.081)

GA.name: Georgia
GA.trNote: Only for trainers identified as agents or employees of a guide, hearing or service dog school, or puppy raisers with credentials from the accredited school. The dog must be leashed and wear that school's identification.
GA.other: Harassing a guide or service dog, or allowing your dog to injure or kill one, is a crime (O.C.G.A. § 16-11-107.1)

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.trNote: State law covers only dogs already individually trained (HRS § 347-2.5); no access right for dogs in training or trainers.
HI.mp: Civil penalty of $100 to $250 for a first violation; at least $500 for later violations
HI.other: Recklessly injuring or killing a service animal on duty is a class C felony (HRS § 711-1109.4); intentionally striking, kicking or poisoning one is a misdemeanor (HRS § 711-1109.5).

ID.name: Idaho
ID.trNote: Anyone accompanying a dog-in-training may enter public accommodations if the dog is leashed and wears a jacket, collar, scarf or similar item identifying it as in training; may be refused if poorly groomed or not under control (Idaho Code § 18-5812B).
ID.mp: Misdemeanor (using a service dog or assistance animal to falsely gain treatment or benefits as a person with a disability)
ID.other: Intentionally interfering with or frightening a service dog is a misdemeanor (Idaho Code § 18-5811); intentionally injuring or killing one is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year in jail and/or a $5,000 fine, plus restitution (§ 18-5812).

IL.name: Illinois
IL.trNote: A person with a disability or a trainer may be accompanied by a dog being trained as a guide, hearing, support or seizure dog (775 ILCS 30/3); 720 ILCS 5/48-8 defines service animal to include animals 'being trained'.
IL.other: Refusing entry to a person with a service animal is a Class C misdemeanor (720 ILCS 5/48-8). Injuring a service animal is a Class 4 felony (Class 3 if it is killed or totally disabled) (510 ILCS 70/4.04).

IN.name: Indiana
IN.trNote: A service animal trainer who is actively training the animal has access; the animal must stay under the trainer's control (IC 16-32-3-2(c)).
IN.other: Knowingly interfering with or mistreating a service animal is a Class A misdemeanor, or a Level 6 felony if it causes serious injury or death (IC 35-46-3-11.5). Housing-only rule: misrepresenting an emotional support animal to a landlord is a Class A infraction (IC 22-9-7-12).

IA.name: Iowa
IA.trNote: A person with a disability, a person assisting them, or a person training a service animal may bring a service-animal-in-training under control (Iowa Code § 216C.11).
IA.other: Knowingly denying or interfering with a service animal user's access rights is a simple misdemeanor (Iowa Code § 216C.11(2)).

KS.name: Kansas
KS.trNote: Only a professional trainer from a recognized training center who is actively training the dog has access (K.S.A. 39-1109).
KS.other: Harming or killing an assistance dog is a crime under K.S.A. 21-6416.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.trNote: Trainers of assistance dogs have access but must carry ID showing they are assistance dog trainers (KRS 258.500, as amended 2024).
KY.mp: Violation with a fine up to $1,000
KY.other: Assault on a service animal is a Class D felony in the first degree (KRS 525.200). A separate housing rule makes misrepresenting an assistance animal a violation with a fine up to $1,000 (KRS 383.085).

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.trNote: A trainer or puppy raiser has the same access rights while the dog is being trained (La. R.S. 46:1955).
LA.mp: Fine up to $500 for a first offense, up to $1,000 for a second, up to $2,500 for a third or later (applies to public accommodations and housing)
LA.other: Denying access to or injuring a service dog is a misdemeanor: $100 to $500 fine and/or up to 6 months in jail (La. R.S. 46:1956).

ME.name: Maine
ME.trNote: A specially trained service dog trainer who is actively training has the same access rights (17 M.R.S. § 1312(4)).
ME.mp: Civil violation with a fine up to $1,000 per occurrence
ME.other: An owner whose dog attacks, injures or kills a working service animal commits a civil violation: forfeiture up to $1,000 plus restitution (7 M.R.S. § 3961-A).

MD.name: Maryland
MD.trNote: A service animal trainer with an animal in training has access, but the animal may be excluded if it creates a clear danger of disturbance or harm (Hum. Servs. § 7-705(c)).
MD.other: Willfully killing or injuring a service animal: up to 2 years and/or $2,500; interfering with a service animal's use: up to 1 year and/or $1,000 (Md. Code, Crim. Law § 10-626).

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.trNote: Anyone raising or training a service dog (including hearing, guide or assistance dogs) has the same access rights as a person with a disability under the ADA (M.G.L. c. 129, § 39F).
MA.other: The handler can sue anyone who steals or attacks an assistance animal for vet bills and the cost of a replacement trained animal (M.G.L. c. 272, § 85B).

MI.name: Michigan
MI.trNote: Public accommodations must allow a service animal in training when it is with its raiser or trainer. This means anyone raising or training the animal to become a service animal (MCL 750.502c(3)).
MI.mp: Misdemeanor: up to 90 days in jail and/or a fine up to $500 for falsely claiming to have a service animal or service animal in training in any public place
MI.other: Willfully assaulting or getting in the way of a service animal is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 90 days and/or $500 (MCL 750.50a).

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.trNote: Anyone training a dog to be a service dog has the right to be accompanied by it in public places (Minn. Stat. § 256C.02).
MN.mp: Petty misdemeanor for a first offense and misdemeanor for later offenses, for intentionally misrepresenting an animal as a service animal in a place of public accommodation
MN.other: Letting your dog run uncontrolled so that it injures a service animal or keeps it from doing its job is a misdemeanor (Minn. Stat. § 609.226, subd. 4). A separate law bars tenants from misrepresenting a need for a service or support animal (Minn. Stat. § 504B.113).

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.trNote: Only support animal trainers have access with animals in training, meaning professional trainers or volunteers working with a professional trainer (Miss. Code Ann. §§ 43-6-153, 43-6-155(2)).
MS.other: Killing or injuring a service animal is a felony, up to $5,000 and 5 years (Miss. Code Ann. § 97-41-23). Harassing a guide dog is a misdemeanor, up to 90 days and/or $500 (§ 97-41-21). State access law expressly covers veterans with PTSD.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.trNote: Only a trainer from a recognized training center, while training the dog (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 209.152).
MO.mp: Class C misdemeanor (class B for repeat offenses), plus civil liability for actual damages
MO.other: Knowingly or recklessly causing serious injury to or the death of a service dog is a class A misdemeanor. Harassing or chasing a known service dog is a class B misdemeanor (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 209.202). Section 209.204 also separately penalizes misrepresenting an assistance animal in housing.

MT.name: Montana
MT.trNote: A person training a service animal has the same access rights, but the animal in training must wear a leash, collar, cape, harness or backpack stating in writing that it is a service animal in training (Mont. Code Ann. § 49-4-214(3)-(4)).
MT.mp: Misdemeanor, but only after a prior written warning: $50 fine for a first offense, $75-$200 for a second, and $100-$1,000 for a third or later offense, plus possible community service
MT.other: Harassing or harming a service animal is a misdemeanor with a fine up to $1,000 (Mont. Code Ann. § 45-8-227). Taking control of a service animal to deprive its handler is also a crime (§ 45-8-228).

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.trNote: Only a bona fide trainer of a service animal with the animal in training (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 20-127(3)). The term is not defined.
NE.mp: Class III misdemeanor. This covers only a person who is not blind using a guide dog or white cane, not service animals in general.
NE.other: Intentionally injuring, harassing or interfering with a service animal is a Class III misdemeanor (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 28-1009.01).

NV.name: Nevada
NV.trNote: A place of public accommodation may not refuse a person who is training a service animal and is accompanied by it (NRS 651.075(1)(b)).
NV.mp: Misdemeanor, fine up to $500 for fraudulently misrepresenting an animal as a service animal or service animal in training
NV.other: Interfering with a service animal is a gross misdemeanor. Beating one is a category E felony and killing one is a category D felony (NRS 426.790).

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.trNote: Only a service animal trainer while actually training. This covers people employed by or volunteering as raisers for a service animal provider, or an individual trainer helping a disabled person train their own animal (RSA 167-D:1(V), 167-D:6).
NH.mp: Misdemeanor for fitting an animal with service-animal gear to pass it off as a service animal, or for impersonating a person with a disability
NH.other: Willfully interfering with a service animal is a misdemeanor (RSA 167-D:8(III), 167-D:10(I)). Injuring one so it cannot return to service is a class A misdemeanor, and restitution is required (RSA 167-D:10(II)-(III)).

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.trNote: Only a guide or service dog trainer employed by a recognized organization, while actually training (N.J.S.A. 10:5-29.3; 10:5-5(t)).
NJ.mp: Fine of $100-$500. This covers only putting a guide-dog harness on an untrained dog to pass it off as a guide dog, not service animals in general.
NJ.other: Recklessly killing a service or guide dog is a fourth-degree crime, injuring one is a disorderly persons offense, and interfering with one is a petty disorderly persons offense, with full restitution (N.J.S.A. 2C:29-3.2). Businesses that deny access face civil penalties of $250, $500, then $1,000 (N.J.S.A. 10:5-29.11).

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.trNote: State definition of 'qualified service animal' includes dogs and miniature horses that are 'being trained'; access applies when the animal is under the control of an owner, trainer or handler.
NM.mp: Misdemeanor (knowingly presenting an animal as a qualified service animal when it is not)
NM.other: Intentionally interfering with the use of a qualified service animal is a misdemeanor (N.M. Stat. § 28-11-5).

NY.name: New York
NY.trNote: A person engaged in training a dog to aid people with disabilities (while training), and the person with a disability for whom the dog is being trained, have the same access rights (Civ. Rights Law § 47-b). Exec. Law § 296(14) also protects professional trainers.
NY.mp: Narrow: knowingly putting a false guide/service/hearing dog ID tag on a dog is a violation with a fine of at least $25 (higher for repeat offenses; up to 15 days jail for 2+ violations in 5 years). No general 'fake service dog' offense.
NY.other: Harming a service animal is a crime (N.Y. Penal Law §§ 242.10, 242.15).

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.trNote: An animal in training may enter public places for training when accompanied by the person training it and wearing a collar and leash, harness, or cape identifying it as a service animal in training (§ 168-4.2(b)). Trainer is liable for damage.
NC.mp: Class 3 misdemeanor (disguising an animal as a service animal or service animal in training)
NC.other: Willfully killing a service animal is a Class H felony; harming, taunting or obstructing one is also a crime (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 14-163.1).

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.trNote: A trainer may bring a service animal in training into public places only if the trainer notifies an onsite manager, wears photo ID from a nationally recognized training program, and is liable for damage (§ 25-13-02.1).
ND.mp: Infraction (knowingly falsely claiming a pet is a service animal to gain entry to a public place or a housing accommodation)
ND.other: Willfully killing or seriously injuring a service animal is a class C felony; harassing or interfering with a working service animal is a class A misdemeanor (N.D. Cent. Code § 25-13-06).

OH.name: Ohio
OH.trNote: A 'trainer of an assistance dog' has the same access rights; a dog in training must be covered by a liability insurance policy (§ 955.43(B)).
OH.other: Assaulting or harassing an assistance dog is a second-degree misdemeanor, rising to a felony if the dog is seriously harmed or killed (Ohio Rev. Code § 2921.321). Denying access is a fourth-degree misdemeanor (§ 955.43(D)).

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.trNote: Only a dog trainer from a recognized training center, while in the act of training guide, signal or service dogs, has access with a dog being trained.
OK.mp: Misdemeanor (knowingly presenting an animal as a service animal to get disability rights or privileges; amended eff. Nov. 1, 2025)
OK.other: Harming, killing or willfully interfering with a service animal is a misdemeanor (up to $1,000 fine and/or 1 year jail) (Okla. Stat. tit. 21, § 649.3).

OR.name: Oregon
OR.trNote: An 'assistance animal trainer' (any individual with care, custody and control of an animal during a course of training to become an assistance animal) has the same access with the 'assistance animal trainee'.
OR.other: Injuring or interfering with an assistance animal is a Class A misdemeanor (Or. Rev. Stat. § 167.352).

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.trNote: Access protection covers anyone who is training a service, guide or support dog or other aid animal for an individual with a disability.
PA.other: Misrepresenting an animal as an assistance/service animal is penalized only for housing (68 P.S. § 405.6: summary offense, fine up to $1,000). Separately, an owner whose dog kills or maims a guide/service dog without provocation commits a third-degree misdemeanor (18 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 5535).

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.trNote: Every trainer or puppy raiser of a service animal has the same access rights; they are liable for damage during training (§ 40-9.1-2.1).
RI.mp: Civil infraction; up to 30 hours of community service at an organization serving people with disabilities
RI.other: Denying or interfering with service animal rights is a misdemeanor (up to 6 months jail and/or fine of at least $100); anyone who injures a service animal is liable for damages and replacement costs (R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-9.1-3).

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.trNote: A trainer of an assistance or guide dog, while engaged in training, has the same access and may be accompanied by a dog in training (§ 43-33-20(d)).
SC.mp: Civil fine up to $250 (1st offense), $500 (2nd), $1,000 (3rd+); not a criminal offense
SC.other: Interfering with a service animal is a misdemeanor (S.C. Code § 47-3-930); injuring or killing one is punishable by fines and jail (§§ 47-3-940, 47-3-960).

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.trNote: A service animal trainer may bring a service animal in training wearing a collar and leash, harness, or cape identifying it as a service animal in training.
SD.mp: Class 2 misdemeanor (new law, SB 82, effective July 1, 2026; applies in places of public accommodation, dogs only)
SD.other: Maliciously injuring, harassing, distracting or otherwise interfering with a service animal is a Class 1 misdemeanor (SDCL § 40-1-38). Separately, a tenant who gives false disability/assistance-animal documentation can be evicted and owe the landlord up to $1,000 (SDCL § 43-32-36).

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.trNote: A dog guide trainer may bring a dog in training if it is harnessed and/or leashed by the trainer and the trainer shows credentials from an accredited dog-guide training school.
TN.mp: Class B misdemeanor plus 100 hours of community service (covers public accommodations and housing)
TN.other: Knowingly or recklessly harming a service animal is a Class A misdemeanor; knowingly interfering with a service animal's duties is a Class C misdemeanor, with mandatory restitution (Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-14-216). Note: the miniature horse language is in the service-animal definition at § 66-7-111(a) (used by the housing and misrepresentation statutes), not in the public-access statute § 62-7-112, which refers to 'dog guides'.

TX.name: Texas
TX.trNote: A service animal in training may not be denied admittance to a public facility when accompanied by an approved trainer (§ 121.003(i)).
TX.mp: Misdemeanor: fine up to $1,000 plus 30 hours of community service
TX.other: Attacking an assistance animal is a Class A misdemeanor, injuring one is a state jail felony, and killing one is a third-degree felony, with restitution (Tex. Penal Code § 42.091).

UT.name: Utah
UT.trNote: A person without a disability may bring an animal that is in training to become a service animal into public accommodations without extra charge (§ 26B-6-803(2)); no professional-trainer requirement.
UT.mp: Class C misdemeanor for knowingly falsely representing that an animal is a service or support animal
UT.other: Injuring or killing a service animal (or letting your animal do so) is a class A misdemeanor; chasing or harassing one is a class B misdemeanor, with restitution (Utah Code § 76-13-211). A 2026 bill (HB 23) proposing a felony was passed without that penalty change.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.trNote: Public accommodations may not bar an individual who is training an animal to be a service animal for a person with a disability (§ 4502(b)(2)).
VT.other: Recklessly injuring or killing a guide/service dog: up to 2 years and/or $3,000; continuing to interfere after notice: up to 1 year and/or $1,000; interfering without prior notice is a civil violation ($100 first, $250 subsequent) (13 V.S.A. § 355).

VA.name: Virginia
VA.trNote: Dog must be at least 6 months old and in identifying gear (harness, orange leash, vest, or organization jacket), and the handler must be an experienced trainer, be doing continuing training of the dog, or be part of a three-unit service dog team.
VA.mp: Class 4 misdemeanor (fine up to $250) for using a vest, harness, sign or disability ID to pass a dog off as a service/hearing dog to gain public access
VA.other: Willfully interfering with a guide or service dog is a Class 3 misdemeanor; willfully injuring one is a Class 1 misdemeanor (Va. Code § 3.2-6588).

WA.name: Washington
WA.trNote: Any 'service animal trainer' (anyone in control of a dog or miniature horse during its training) may bring the trainee into public areas; it must be tethered unless that interferes with training, and can be removed if out of control or not housebroken.
WA.other: Interfering with a service animal is a misdemeanor (gross misdemeanor if repeated); recklessly injuring or killing one is a gross misdemeanor; intentionally doing so is a class C felony (RCW 9.91.170).

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.trNote: Access rights extend to a person certified as a trainer of a service animal while engaged in training (§ 5-15-4(d)).
WV.mp: Misdemeanor: up to $200 fine and/or 10 days in jail; second or later offense up to $1,000 and/or 30 days

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.trNote: A service animal trainer may be admitted if the animal wears a harness or leash and special cape; the business may ask for certification from a school for training service animals.
WI.other: Housing only: misrepresenting a disability or need for an emotional support animal to a landlord brings a forfeiture of at least $500 (Wis. Stat. § 106.50(2r)(br)5). Interfering with, injuring or killing a service dog ranges from a Class B misdemeanor to a Class H felony (Wis. Stat. § 951.097). 2025 bills for a public misrepresentation penalty (AB 366 / SB 327) were not enacted.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.trNote: The state definition of service animal includes a dog being trained to do work or tasks for a person with a disability (§ 35-13-205(a)(viii)); the statute has no separate trainer provision or gear requirement.
WY.mp: Misdemeanor, fine up to $750 (covers service and assistance animals)
WY.other: Knowingly causing serious harm, permanent disability or death to a service or assistance animal is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year and/or $5,000, with restitution (Wyo. Stat. § 35-13-206).

PR.name: Puerto Rico
PR.law: Ley Núm. 51 of May 29, 1970, as amended
PR.trNote: Puerto Rico’s law doesn’t cover dogs in training, and neither does the federal ADA.
PR.other: Puerto Rico’s law requires a trainer’s certification and a yearly vet certificate. Those requirements are stricter than the ADA, which also applies in Puerto Rico. Under the ADA, a business still can’t demand papers at the door. Denying access is a misdemeanor under the local law.

GU.name: Guam
GU.trNote: Guam’s law doesn’t cover dogs in training, and neither does the federal ADA.
GU.other: Guam’s law covers guide dogs for people who are blind, and denying access is a misdemeanor. Other service dogs are protected by the federal ADA, which applies in Guam.

VI.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
VI.law: Federal ADA (42 U.S.C. §12103(2)); 10 V.I.C. § 64 (general disability discrimination)
VI.trNote: We found no territorial law covering dogs in training. The federal ADA doesn’t cover them.
VI.other: We found no territorial law specific to service animals. The federal ADA applies, and local law bans disability discrimination in general.

AS.name: American Samoa
AS.trNote: We found no territorial law covering dogs in training. The federal ADA doesn’t cover them.
AS.other: We found no territorial law specific to service animals. The federal ADA applies.

MP.name: Northern Mariana Islands
MP.trNote: We found no territorial law covering dogs in training. The federal ADA doesn’t cover them.
MP.other: We found no territorial law specific to service animals. The federal ADA applies.
